steps.title: Use a permitted copy and your matching game files
steps.instruction: Keep an existing permitted complete native player, including its resources and libraries. The Windows player is MikuPan.exe; register it with its folder as the working directory. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. Prepare your own IMG_HD.BIN and IMG_BD.BIN from the matching Fatal Frame disc in a separate retained data folder. Default upstream builds use NTSC-U USA; PAL/EU needs the matching EU build, and the Japanese edition is unsupported. No original files or PS2 BIOS are supplied by Portcove.

steps.title: Choose the original-data folder on first Play
steps.instruction: The native player asks for the folder containing the missing game files on first deliberate Play and remembers your selection. Keep that original-data folder outside any separately managed runtime so replacing a player does not replace your originals. The package is portable and has no installer. Source builds have their own CMake/dependency instructions. Linux is a separate upstream route; macOS is an experimental Apple Silicon community build with no maintained hardware coverage, not Windows qualification.

steps.title: Back up the actual profile before updating
steps.instruction: You or upstream update this external copy. Close the game, keep the working folder, and extract a new permitted player separately. Back up the SDL profile for Mikompilation/MikuPan, including mikupan.ini, memory-card saves, albums and PNG captures; on Windows this is normally under AppData/Roaming. If SDL cannot supply a profile directory, upstream uses the local MikuPan directory instead; retain that too. Preserve the original-data folder separately. External registration leaves every file untouched and provides no managed Update, Backup or Rollback. Runtime replacement does not rewind saves or establish older-version readability.
